newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine ends ban on grain movement-trade.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine ends ban on grain movement-trade.

text.p: Grain within Ukraine is moving freely again after many regions refused to release it earlier this month until state grain orders were met, Western experts said on Tuesday.
"The bans are pretty well off," said Bohdan Chomiak of Chemonics International, a U.S.-funded group working to develop the agriculture sector in the former Soviet republic.
"Everyone raised a hue and cry and they were successful this year," he said.

This year's limits on grain movement recalled a situation a year ago, when grain exchanges stopped working and many trading companies lost money after the government quietly ordered grain to remain in silos until state orders were filled.

Ukraine has promised to do away with the Soviet-era practice of grain buying by the state, often at below-market prices, next year. This year's order was set at 5.88 million tonnes against 5.00 million tonnes in 1996.
Ukraine has forecast a grain harvest of 37-38 million tonnes this year compared to 25.4 million tonnes in 1996.

U.S. ambassador to Ukraine William Miller, who lobbied on behalf of U.S. companies denied pre-purchased grain this year, said President Leonid Kuchma, Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko and Agriculture Minister Yuri Karasyk had promised to ensure grain would be released.
"They have given the order that there be open trade in these matters," Miller told Reuters.
The government has never formally admitted to issuing orders last year placing bans on grain movements, but top officials have promised such bans would never happen again.
